dedupe_keys.name: switzerland heat and emergency hospital admissions of older adults receiving home care 2019 to 2022

description: This case study assesses how hot weather raises the risk of emergency hospital admission among older adults who receive home care services in Switzerland, and which personal characteristics change that risk. The authors, at the Institute of Social and Preventive Medicine of the University of Bern, linked patient-level emergency admission data to daily maximum temperature in each MedStat region of residence and used a case time series design with quasi-Poisson regression and distributed lag non-linear models; the work is deposited open access in the University of Bern repository. Coverage is Switzerland, 2019 to 2022, by MedStat region. The repository copy is free to read; the patient data are not public. Caveats: exposure is regional temperature, not indoor conditions, and the cohort covers home care recipients only. The study found an overall heat-related admission risk of 1.12 at the 99th temperature percentile compared with the minimum-risk temperature, higher for men (1.16) than women (1.09) except among those aged 85 and over; dependency, anxiety, dementia, cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and coronary heart disease modified the risk differently for women and men. Simulation uses: heat-driven demand parameters for hospital and emergency service capacity models in ageing populations. Related records: the British Columbia heatwave simulation (case_study-british-columbia-2021-heatwave-acute-care-des) models the effect of a heat surge on acute care.
